Super Micro CEO Calls a $72 Billion to $82 Billion Outlook "Very, Very Conservative" ©@Tiero via Canva
Key Takeaways

Super Micro raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion, from $65 billion to $72 billion, and its CEO says even the new range is conservative.

To reach the low end, Super Micro needs less revenue per quarter than it made in its first quarter once a one-time catch-up is taken out.

CFO Mark Long says the pace of customers' data center construction sets the range, and he names land, power and building shells as the industry's binding constraints, which also hold back the Nvidia-powered racks Super Micro ships.

At 4.7x forward earnings, investors are pricing in a miss, and the risk to watch is data center construction, including a possible moratorium in Texas.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) just raised its outlook for the year, and its CEO thinks the new one is still too low.

On its fiscal first-quarter call, Super Micro raised its revenue outlook for the year ending June 2027 to $72 billion to $82 billion, from $65 billion to $72 billion. An analyst asked what was holding back the second half. CEO Charles Liang pointed to shortages of key components and the economy, and said that if neither turns into a big problem, the second half will be "much bigger than our first half."

"And if that's the case, $72 billion to $82 billion becomes very, very conservative."

That's two big ifs. Investors weren't convinced either: shares sank 11% in a week despite a $4 billion beat.

But CFO Mark Long added a third limit: the buildings Super Micro's servers go into. That reaches Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) too.

Liang has the numbers on his side

Analysts have already moved to the middle of the new range. The fiscal 2027 consensus is $76.9 billion from 15 analysts, after revenue grew from $14.9 billion in fiscal 2024 to $39.1 billion in fiscal 2026:

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to June) (TIKR)

The quarter Super Micro just reported makes the low end look very reachable. Revenue was $19.9 billion in the September quarter. Long said about $2.3 billion of that was catch-up from earlier deployments, which leaves about $17.6 billion of underlying revenue.

To reach $72 billion, Super Micro needs $52.1 billion over the next three quarters, or about $17.4 billion a quarter. That's less than the underlying business just did. Long said the range still assumes "continued sequential growth in underlying demand," so the bottom of it leaves plenty of room for things to go wrong. The second-half outlook also doesn't count on significant growth in selling prices, even though Long said key component costs have been rising "sometimes more than quarterly."

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.6 indicates a change of +12.2% from what Super Micro is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +9.1%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
detail:
Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
Decrypt Staff

META
AAPL
MSFT
GOOG
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Every member of Wall Street's "Magnificent Seven" now wants its stock kept off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Apple and Meta Platforms are among 11 companies added to the list of objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Thursday.

They join Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia and Tesla, completing a sweep by the group of tech giants that makes up a large share of the S&P 500's value. The other new objectors are Home Depot, Boeing, GE Vernova, Palantir, ServiceNow, S&P Global, KLA, Super Micro Computer and Nebius Group, bringing the total number of companies saying "no" to the OKX and ICE platform to 67.

Meta's objection carries some irony. The Facebook parent once tried to launch its own stablecoin, Libra, later renamed Diem, before abandoning the project in 2022 amid regulatory pushback.

Apple had been one of the last megacaps missing from the list after Amazon, Tesla, and SpaceX objected in the venue's Nov. 2 notice. The tally stood at 56 then, and at nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

Just as notable is who hasn't objected. Crypto-friendly public companies such as Coinbase, Robinhood and Strategy don't appear on the list. Coinbase launched tokenized stocks for non-U.S. users on its Base network in August. Berkshire Hathaway, Visa, and Exxon Mobil are also absent. It's unclear whether OKXICE notified those companies.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act failed to advance in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. It's worth noting, though, that the objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain. An outside "tokenizer" would hold real shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer.

With the market's biggest names opted out, it's unclear which major stocks the venue will be able to offer at launch, and its notices don't list the tokens it plans to make available.

title: Despite Strong Revenue Growth and a Cheap Valuation, Supermicro Stock Is Still Not a Buy
detail:
Despite Strong Revenue Growth and a Cheap Valuation, Supermicro Stock Is Still Not a Buy
Geoffrey Seiler, The Motley Fool

SMCI
DELL
HPE
NVDA

Trading disclosure

With a long history of controversy, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) is one of the most divisive stocks in the market. The company has been growing revenue quickly and remains a clear beneficiary of the AI build-out. However, it also has a history of accounting issues, and three now-former employees have been charged by the Department of Justice with violating U.S. technology export bans. As such, the stock is down by more than 35% over the past year, while rivals Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise have more than doubled over the same period.

Supermicro designs and assembles servers and rack solutions for data centers. It normally customizes its systems around Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), and provides turnkey solutions that include things like networking, cooling, and software. The company has said its big advantage is speed, as its integrated rack solutions get customers up and running more quickly.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Despite being a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out, Supermicro has dealt with a lot of issues over the past few years. A short-seller accused the company of accounting irregularities in 2024, and the subsequent investigations eventually led to the company's auditor resigning and delays in its regulatory filings. This was preceded by the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) fining the company in 2020 for improperly recognizing revenue, and in 2018, the stock was delisted from the Nasdaq after the company failed to file financial reports. It did not relist on the exchange until 2020.

The biggest issue the company faces currently, however, is that three former employees, including one of its co-founders, have been charged with illegally smuggling high-end Nvidia GPUs into China through an elaborate scheme that involved fake paperwork, "dummy" servers, and a Thailand-based company that acted as an intermediary. Throughout all these scandals, somehow, CEO Charles Liang has managed to stay in charge.

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Strong growth and outlook

While the company has dealt with a lot of controversy, it has also produced some strong growth this calendar year.

In its fiscal 2027 first quarter (which ended Sept. 30), Supermicro's revenue nearly quadrupled year over year from $5 billion to $19.9 billion. That was well above the $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion range that management forecast in August.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) had an earnings quarter that, at first blush, you may think investors would be celebrating. Revenue nearly quadrupled, earnings easily beat expectations, and management raised its full-year sales forecast. All good things, right?

Instead, Supermicro stock ended trading down nearly 4% Wednesday, as investors look beyond the impressive numbers and focus on some troubling developments underneath them.

And I think their skepticism is justified. There's a shadow over Supermicro stock, and Tuesday's fiscal first-quarter earnings report did nothing to shake it.

Thursday's broad selloff in chipmakers and AI stocks hasn't been helping SMCI's case either.

Supermicro's AI Business Is Booming

There's no question that Supermicro is benefiting from the massive investments companies are making in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

The company manufactures servers and provides integrated data center solutions, including liquid cooling systems. Its products are used to build the facilities that power AI applications, making Supermicro a direct beneficiary of growing demand for computing capacity.

In its fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended Sept. 30, Supermicro reported revenue of $19.9 billion, up 298% from a year ago. Adjusted earnings reached $1.81 per share, easily beating Wall Street's expectations of $1.24.

www.barchart.com

AI-related solutions accounted for roughly 71% of quarterly revenue, up from 59% in the previous quarter.

And management expects the momentum to continue. Supermicro raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to between $72 billion and $82 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $65 billion to $72 billion. For the current quarter, it expects revenue of $19.5 billion to $21.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.66 to $1.90 per share.

Those are outstanding growth figures. But there's a problem.

More Revenue Isn't Necessarily Translating Into Better Margins

Supermicro's non-GAAP gross margin fell to 12.8% in the quarter, which is an improvement from 9.5% a year ago, but also is down from 17.6% in the preceding quarter.

Key Takeaways

Super Micro Computer fell 10% today with no company news, as AI hardware selling continued after Democrats' midterm wins.

Celestica, ASE Technology and Everpure fell harder on fears that data center building could slow.

Two days earlier, Super Micro raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion.

At less than half its usual forward P/E, Super Micro is priced for a slowdown, though its cash burn is a real risk.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% today, and nothing the company said explains it. The AI hardware selloff that began Wednesday, after Democrats' bigger-than-expected midterm wins, deepened this morning.

Celestica (CLS) fell 13%, chip packager ASE Technology (ASX) dropped 17% and storage maker Everpure (P:NYSE) slid 15%, with no news of their own. All three sell into the same data center buildout.

Investors shrugged off a raised outlook

On Tuesday, Super Micro reported $19.9 billion of September-quarter revenue and raised its fiscal 2027 outlook (the year ending June 2027) to $72 billion to $82 billion. Going in, analysts expected $70.3 billion for fiscal 2027 and $81.7 billion for fiscal 2028:

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (years to June) (TIKR)

So the top of the new range is about what analysts had penciled in for a year later.

Investors are worried about Texas

Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who promised a data center moratorium, unseated Texas Gov. Greg Abbott on Tuesday. Texas holds more than a quarter of the US data center capacity planned through 2030, according to Yahoo Finance. Data center developer Applied Digital (APLD:NASDAQ) fell 16% today on fears about permits.

Super Micro needs its biggest customers to keep building: one made up 44% of September-quarter revenue. Inventory rose to $15.1 billion at Sept. 30, from $12.9 billion in June.

Super Micro Computer SMCI shares have lost 5.7% since it released its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 3, 2026. The stock has plunged 31.9% in the past one month, underperforming the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry and the sector's decline of 13.2% and 24.7%, respectively.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The decline in stock price has led SMCI stock to trade at a discounted price-to-sales multiple of 0.27X, below its industry's P/S of 2.19X. The undervaluation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of B.

SMCI Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Given these dynamics, investors are wondering if it's the right time to buy, sell or hold SMCI stock. Let's delve deeper into the fundamentals, growth drivers, competitive positioning, valuation and risks surrounding the company to better assess its long-term investment potential.

SMCI Stock Declines in Tune With the Broader Technology Market

The decline in SMCI's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since SMCI supplies its products to these infrastructure providers, SMCI's stock has also been affected.

Furthermore, the recent decline after the earnings can mainly be attributed to investors assessing the sustainability of its rapid revenue growth and the pressure on profitability. The company reported record net sales of $19.95 billion, up 298% year over year and 79% sequentially. However, gross margin declined to 12.7% from 17.5% in the preceding quarter, while non-GAAP gross margin fell 480 basis points sequentially to 12.8%.

Management attributed the decline primarily to an increase in AI-related revenue mix, which rose to 71% from 59% in the previous quarter. Large-scale AI data center deployments carry lower gross margins than the more diversified enterprise and channel businesses, while the recognition of certain lower-margin deferred revenues further weighed on profitability.

Investor concerns were also heightened by Super Micro Computer's high customer concentration. During the quarter, one large data center customer accounted for 44% of total revenue compared with 28% for fiscal 2026 as a whole. Additionally, two customers represented 49% and 17% of accounts receivable at the end of the quarter. However, Super Micro Computer's exposure to AI infrastructure continues to provide a powerful foundation for growth.
